# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Mid-forties in Volume 1; forty-five by the time of her marriage.  <sub>[v1 c19 P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 c21 P11](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0011)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive and married  <sub>[v1 c28 P39](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0039), [v1 c29 P8](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c21 P0](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0000), [v1 c21 P12](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0012)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker  <sub>[v1 c21 P12](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0012)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Penrose  <sub>[v1 c19 P78](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0078)</sub>; Mrs. Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c29 P8](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a short, slender woman with thick, wavy, snow-white hair arranged in flattering puffs and coils. Her youthful, rosy-cheeked face features dimples and large, gentle, wood-brown eyes with golden flecks. She prefers light, delicate dresses adorned with frills and laces.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 c20 P20](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0020), [v1 c21 P9](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0009), [v1 c23 P10](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0010)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses a playful, imaginative, and romantic nature, enjoying daydreams and pretend games as much as a young girl. Though she carries a deep capacity for affection and warmth, her youthful pride and moodiness once caused her great sorrow. She has a gentle, sensitive soul that is deeply attuned to beauty and small delights.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097), [v1 c21 P19](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0019), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and romantic  <sub>[v1 c19 P86](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0086), [v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097)</sub>
- Proud and moody in youth  <sub>[v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Kindred spirit to dreamers  <sub>[v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097)</sub>

## Abilities

- Gardening  <sub>[v1 c21 P53](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0053)</sub>
- Creating echo games  <sub>[v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)</sub>

## Goals

- To find joy and companionship through imagination despite her solitary life  <sub>[v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053), [v1 c19 P85](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0085)</sub>
- To reunite with her youthful love, Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 c23 P21](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0021)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose grew up at Echo Cottage, a secluded stone house in Middle Welby. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but her pride and a silly argument caused them to part ways, after which Stephen moved to the United States and she remained single. She lived a quiet, imaginative life at Echo Cottage alongside a series of young hired girls whom she collectively called Belinda. When Nell Harcourt visited her after a bed-jumping incident, Rosalind formed a warm bond with her and later welcomed Stephen's young son, Cedric, into her heart. Encouraged by Nell, Stephen visited Echo Cottage years after his first wife's death, leading to a reconciliation. Rosalind married Stephen in her garden beneath the honeysuckle trellis and subsequently moved to Boston, returning periodically to spend summers at Echo Cottage.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053), [v1 c19 P76](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0076), [v1 c19 P81](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0081), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c23 P27](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0027), [v1 c28 P39](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0039), [v1 c29 P8](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0008), [v1 c29 P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## Background by volume

- Born to parents who named her Rosalind because of her father's love for lavender  <sub>[v1 c29 P26](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0026)</sub>
- Grew up in a stone cottage built by her father at Echo Cottage in Middle Welby  <sub>[v1 c19 P85](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0085), [v1 c21 P48](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0048)</sub>
- Was engaged in her youth to Stephen Stanhope before a foolish quarrel separated them  <sub>[v1 c23 P15](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0015), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018)</sub>
- Lived a solitary life taking in a series of young hired girls named Belinda  <sub>[v1 c19 P76](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am aware you will consider me terribly silly. I am silly . . . and I feel humiliated about it whenever I am caught, but only when I am caught.  <sub>[v1 c21 P53](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0053)</sub>

> I could never feel affection for anyone else, nor did I desire to. I was certain I would prefer being an unmarried woman for ten centuries over marrying anyone who was not Stephen Stanhope.  <sub>[v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>

> I take it back—I’m not old. And I’m not going to be old. I’m going to pretend I’m seventeen too, now you’re here, Nell.  <sub>[v1 c23 P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)</sub>
